name: Nighty Blender
author: NightyCode
description: Your Blender, for the AI in Nighty Vault: import a model, make it game-ready (exact triangle count, UVs, textures, checks, export for Roblox and other engines). No AI model inside: models come from you.

mcp.note: Nighty Blender drives the person's own Blender (4.2+), paired in Nighty Vault's Blender card. Models come from the person's file, an import, or code only when the person asks: there is no AI model in it and it never generates one. Start with blender_status; read blender_guide { topic: "workflow" } once. New file: blender_import, then blender_make_game_ready (ask its one options question first). Slow tools answer with a job id: blender_job { action: "wait" }. Each change is one undo step "AI: ..."; blender_undo takes back only yours. The safety level is the person's, set in Blender only.

tools.name: check
tools.description: Checks, by what: mesh (counts, open / non-manifold edges, floating parts, flipped normals, UV overlap and stretch; pass, errors, warnings), textures (the baked maps: blur, metallic 0/1, baked-in light, unbaked pixels), source (the model against its locked _SOURCE copy: size, triangles, surface drift), roundtrip (export, read back, compare: what the engine gets), roblox (the Roblox gate: 20,000 triangles per part, UVs, 1024 px maps, scale, an export), final (marks the asset finished; refuses unless the last mesh check passed and nothing changed since, or a stated reason).

names.description: (mesh, source, roundtrip, roblox, final) Required for final. Object names (default: the selected objects, else every visible mesh). / The asset's objects.

allow_open.description: (mesh) Open surfaces are fine (planes, leaves, cards).

allow_floating.description: (mesh) Objects that may float on purpose (a hanging lamp, a hover part).

budget.description: (mesh) Most triangles allowed over all objects.

full.description: (mesh) Every number per object (default: the ones that matter).

tolerance_pct.description: (source) Most drift allowed (95% of points), in % of the size (default 1).

file.description: (roundtrip) An exported file to read back (default: a temporary GLB).

reason.description: (final) Why finishing without a passing check is right.

notes.description: (final) What it is, for the record (one line).

tools.name: export
tools.description: Exports for an engine with the right scale, axes, normal-map format and channel packing: roblox (SurfaceAppearance maps, studs), unity (URP / HDRP maps), unreal (ORM, DirectX normal, cm), godot / gltf (.glb), blender (.blend). Bakes first when needed. Slow: a job.

tools.name: guide
tools.description: Know-how. No arguments: the guide topics. topic: one guide (start with workflow: import first). examples: words to find verified example scripts (only when the person asked for a model built in code). api: this Blender's own API for a type, property or operator (bpy.types.Object, Mesh.vertices, bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add): look names up instead of guessing.

topic.description: A guide topic (workflow, blender-api, topology, texturing, ...).

examples.description: Words for the example search, e.g. 'wooden crate'.

image.description: examples: add the best match's render.

api.description: A bpy type, property or operator.

tools.name: import
tools.description: Brings the person's model file in (GLB, glTF, FBX or OBJ, full path) as one object through a background Blender, keeps a locked <name>_SOURCE copy (never changed; check { what: source } compares against it) and writes a triage report (triangles, open edges, loose parts, UVs, textures, scale, rigs: what it needs). Optional fixes: level, facing, metal. A job: job { action: wait }.

file.description: Full path of the model file.

size.description: Longest side in meters (default: as stored in the file).

fixes.description: Optional: level (stand it upright), facing (long side along X, front +X), metal (make a guessed metal map exactly 0/1).

tools.name: job
tools.description: Slow work (imports, bakes, renders, exports, make_game_ready) runs as a job: the call answers with { job: id } at once. action wait: wait up to 45 s for it, then its result (or its progress: wait again); cancel: stop it; get: its state now; list: every job.

tools.name: look
tools.description: Pictures of the model from fixed views (default front, right, top and a 3/4 view) in one image, plus each camera's pose. mode: solid (material colors), matcap (form and shading errors), material (studio render: real materials, soft lights, ground shadow, rendered by a background Blender), silhouette. View "hero" picks the best 3/4 angle. wireframe: true draws the edges on top. Off-screen: the view and settings stay as they are, and Blender keeps running while it renders. A render that takes longer than 40 s answers with a job id: then job { action: wait }. Use it after every change.

names.description: Object names (default: the selected objects, else every visible mesh).

views.description: Default [front, right, top, three_quarter]. Front looks from -Y.

perspective.description: Front / side / top in perspective (default ortho).

separate.description: One picture per view instead of a grid.

references.description: Draw loaded reference pictures behind (ortho views).

tools.name: make_game_ready
tools.description: The full pipeline as one job on the person's model: a file (imported first, with a locked _SOURCE copy and a triage report) or a mesh in the scene. Cleanup, clean colors, the exact triangle count, parts, UVs, textures (its own re-baked, or library materials per part), texture check, export for the engine, mesh check, finish. Ask first: without confirmed: true and the picks it starts nothing and answers with the ONE question to send the person (ask: true gives it at once); on their OK call again with their picks in options and confirmed: true. A job (job { action: wait }, minutes). Fixes after: mesh / texture.

file.description: A model file on this PC to start from (GLB, glTF, FBX or OBJ; full path). It is imported first, with a locked _SOURCE copy.

object.description: Or a mesh already in the scene (imported before, or built in code when the person asked for that).

size.description: With file: longest side in meters (default: the file's own size).

confirmed.description: true only after the person answered the options question (OK or their changes). Without it nothing starts: the answer is the question to ask.

options.description: The picks the person confirmed (override the preset): mesh auto / triangles / quads, faces (the exact triangle count), detail low / medium / high, textures none / color / pbr / stylized, texture_type baked / blender, size 1K / 2K / 4K, made_for roblox / unity / unreal / godot / gltf / blender, colors auto / clean / keep

faces.description: The exact triangle count (used as given).

colors.description: the model's colors: auto (clean flat colors with crisp borders when the texture is mostly flat colors, else only metal / roughness per region), clean, keep

texture_source.description: own: the model's own textures re-baked onto the low poly; materials: real library materials per part, picked from each part's own colors; auto (default): materials when materials are given, else own.

materials.description: Library materials to choose from, e.g. ['wood', 'brass'] (biggest part first).

split.description: Split into parts (default: only for materials per part).

cleanup.description: Clean the mesh first (weld, floaters, holes; default: yes for a file, no for a scene mesh).

path.description: Export folder (default next to the .blend / Blender's folder).

ask.description: Only the options question for these picks (with options / preset; starts nothing).

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Sizes in meters: each object's bounds (size, min, max, center), the group's, optional distances between pairs (surface gap, touching) and a comparison with a reference or ghost object (size ratio, overlap, average surface distance).

names.description: Object names (default: the selected objects, else every visible mesh).

pairs.description: [[a, b], ...] object pairs to measure the distance between.

reference.description: A reference / ghost object to compare the objects with.

tools.name: mesh
tools.description: Mesh steps on the working model (never on a _SOURCE copy), by op: cleanup (weld, floaters, holes, manifold, normals, size, on the ground), decimate (an exact triangle count, keeps sharp edges, seams, symmetry), retopo (quads, triangles or auto; exact counts), uv_unwrap (one shared atlas, seams from sharp edges), lods (_LOD1.. copies), split_parts (by loose pieces, creases, planes or color regions), fix_shading (normals out, smooth with sharp edges by angle). Each is one undo step; the slow ones answer with a job id (job { action: wait }).

objects.description: Mesh object names. Default: the selected meshes, else the active object. / Object names (default: the selected objects, else every visible mesh).

size.description: (cleanup) Real size in meters along size_axis (e.g. 0.9 for a rifle).

floaters.description: (cleanup) Remove loose pieces smaller than this share of the whole size (0 = keep).

manifold.description: (cleanup) auto: targeted fixes, voxel rebuild only if still broken.

voxel_size.description: (cleanup) Meters (default: picked from the size and detail).

join.description: (cleanup) Join parts left floating a few mm apart (common in generated models) into one solid.

flatten.description: (cleanup) Make flat sides truly flat with crisp edges (auto: hard-surface shapes only).

faces.description: (decimate, retopo, lods) Target triangles. / Exact face count (overrides detail).

sharp_angle.description: (decimate, retopo) Degrees; sharper edges stay crisp.

keep_source.description: (decimate, retopo) Keep the dense original hidden for baking.

detail.description: (retopo) low ~3k, medium ~12k, high ~40k triangles (quads: half as many faces).

engine.description: (retopo) Quad remesher (auto: the best one installed).

seam_angle.description: (uv_unwrap) Degrees; sharper crease lines become seams.

shared.description: (uv_unwrap) One atlas for all objects (one texture set).

angle.description: (split_parts, fix_shading) Degrees for concave / sharp. / Edges sharper than this stay sharp (degrees, default 30).

planes.description: (split_parts) For method plane: cut planes in object space.

min_size.description: (split_parts) Regions under this share of the surface join a neighbour.

cap.description: (split_parts) Close the cut openings (default: only for plane).

clear.description: (fix_shading) Remove custom split normals first (default true).

tools.name: reference
tools.description: Reference pictures for modeling: load puts pictures as scaled image planes aligned to a view (shown in ortho views, never rendered; the subject's size in meters from width or height); score renders the model's silhouette in that view and compares (overlap IoU, sizes, a picture: red = model only, blue = reference only); list; clear.

path.description: A picture file on this computer (PNG / JPG).

view.description: The view it shows (front looks from -Y: a gun along X shows its side).

center.description: Subject center on the view plane (u, v) in meters.

names.description: Object names (default: the selected objects, else every visible mesh).

tools.name: run_python
tools.description: Run a short Python script in Blender (bpy, bmesh, mathutils, math, random, nighty ready). For small fixes the person asked for; models come from the person's file (build one in code only when the person asks for that). `result` is returned; print() is captured. 'safe' level: no imports or risky calls; 'full': any.

tools.name: scene
tools.description: The scene as a compact tree: collections, objects (type, location, size, faces, modifiers, materials, children), selection, units and Blender version. Call it first.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Nighty Blender in the person's Blender: pairing state, Blender and addon versions, the safety level the person set (tools / safe Python / full Python; only they can change it, in Blender's N panel), the open .blend file and the jobs still running. A good first call.

tools.name: texture
tools.description: Texture steps, by op: bake (the parts' materials or the model's own textures into clean maps, one texture set; a job), clean_colors (an imported model's ragged texture colors made flat and crisp per region, or only metal / roughness fixed when it has real detail; a job), stylize (hand-painted look), decal (a sharp image or text projected on a part), assign_materials (real library materials per part: steel, wood, rubber...; CC0 texture downloads only after the person agrees), fix_seams (texture colors grown past UV edges: no lines along seams).

parts.description: (bake, stylize, assign_materials, fix_seams) Required for assign_materials. {part: 'gunmetal'} or {part: {material, color '#rrggbb', force_tint (tint wood / leather too), wear, dirt, roughness}} / Object names (default: the selected objects, else every visible mesh).

size.description: (bake, clean_colors, decal) The final texture size (default from asset_options): details it can't show go. / width in meters

high.description: (bake) {low part: high poly} for normal / AO from a high poly

from_high.description: (bake) Colors / roughness / metallic from the high poly's own textures (an imported model's) instead of the parts' materials

objects.description: (clean_colors) Models (default: selected, else every imported model).

picture.description: (clean_colors) A picture of the object (full path, optional): fixes colors that drifted in the texture (white gone lavender).

image.description: (decal) a PNG / JPG path (or give text)

at.description: (decal) a world point instead of side

outline.description: (decal) text outline, share of its height (0.06)

remove.description: (decal) name of a decal to remove

cc0.description: (assign_materials) use CC0 photo textures (Poly Haven) where the library has them

cc0_agree.description: (assign_materials) the person said yes to CC0 downloads

margin_px.description: (fix_seams) How far to grow, in pixels (default 1/64 of the size).

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Takes back the AI's own changes only (steps named 'AI: ...'); it stops at the person's own work and never undoes it. No arguments: the last AI step. steps: several. checkpoint: a named mark to come back to; to: back to that mark. list: the recent steps.

steps.description: How many AI steps to take back (1-50, default 1).

checkpoint.description: Set a named checkpoint now (nothing is undone).

to.description: Undo the AI's steps back to this checkpoint.
